concept: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The mongodb-atlas-local image is an evaluation and CI option, not a production exit target: MongoDB describes it as single-node without high availability and directs production users to separate supported deployment paths. Local query success alone does not validate a production migration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Moving database documents does not establish application portability: Databasezy explicitly excludes Atlas Search indexes and triggers from its Atlas copy workflow, while MongoDB documents Atlas Triggers as logic that runs linked Atlas Functions in response to database events or schedules. Treat service replacement as a separate exit-work item. Sources: https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers.md

Atlas database Triggers run outside the database server on a serverless compute layer, consume change streams, and invoke Atlas Functions or forward events to AWS EventBridge. Exporting collection data alone does not reproduce that execution service; this exit implication is an architectural inference from the documented design. (low confidence)

Atlas database Triggers execute on a serverless compute layer that scales independently of the database server, and each database Trigger is built on a change stream. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md

A practical exit assessment should inventory Search operators and index definitions, trigger functions and schedules, and the operational services the destination must supply. This is a methodological inference from documented feature exceptions and migration omissions. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md ; https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers.md

The documented feature boundary remains uneven: $rerank is Atlas-only. An application using that stage needs an alternative implementation when leaving Atlas; Percona describes its alternative as a plan. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md ; https://www.percona.com/?p=51371

Databasezy documents its Atlas migration as a copy-only mongodump-to-mongorestore workflow, without continuous synchronization, and explicitly says it does not copy Search indexes or triggers. This limitation describes that migration tool; it does not prove those features are intrinsically impossible to recreate elsewhere. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-28)

Search and Vector Search are no longer categorically Atlas-only. MongoDB documents self-managed Community and Enterprise deployment paths; its mongot repository offers a Community Search image. Percona independently reports that self-managed search reached GA in July 2026 and describes its downstream Technical Preview. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/ ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongot ; https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb

The self-managed limitations documentation lists $search, $searchMeta, $vectorSearch, and Search index helper methods as available on both platforms, but lists $rerank as Atlas-only, excludes nestedRoot index syntax on self-managed mongot, and notes differences in $listSearchIndexes output. Portability therefore requires checking the exact feature surface. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Leaving managed Search transfers operational work to the operator. MongoDB assigns provisioning, upgrades, security patching, alerting, logs, recovery supervision, and capacity management to self-managed deployments; Percona separately identifies gaps in the surrounding automation and observability. These are concrete engineering tasks, not a universal dollar estimate for exit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md ; https://www.percona.com/?p=51371

Search is no longer categorically Atlas-only: MongoDB publishes self-managed mongot deployment paths and source code, and Percona distributes the same underlying engine independently. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/ ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongot ; https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb

MongoDB documents $search, $searchMeta and $vectorSearch on both platforms. Moving off Atlas therefore does not inherently require replacing the search engine; compatibility still needs workload testing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

mongot is source-available under SSPL v1. Percona uses the same license and explicitly distinguishes it from OSI-approved open source; self-hostability alone does not establish unrestricted hosted-service redistribution rights. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongot/blob/main/README.md ; https://www.percona.com/?p=51371 ; https://www.infoworld.com/article/4118081
